speakers.evidence: "Ken, there was a note from Lisa Shelter" addressed at row #37; Ken responds throughout as staff

speakers.name: Melinda
speakers.evidence: "Melinda." addressed by chair at row #56, and she responds as staff presenter

speakers.name: Annie Spencer
speakers.evidence: "We are William and Annie Spencer, living at 1171 Ledgewood Drive." (row #54)

chapters.title: Opening of Meeting
chapters.summary: Board chair opens the DRB meeting for August 8, listing three agenda items to review.

chapters.title: Lakeview Farm Inc. Discretionary Permit
chapters.summary: Staff presents a two-lot subdivision request in the ARZD; discussion covers open space set-aside, conservation commission recommendations on wetlands and building envelope location, plantings, and state permits obtained.

chapters.title: Building Envelope and Plantings Confirmation
chapters.summary: Board and applicant's engineer confirm the building envelope was moved 50 feet as previously recommended, and additional plantings were added on Lot 1 per conservation commission guidance.

chapters.title: Lisa Shelter's Utility Comments
chapters.summary: Staff notes utility department comments requiring underground utilities, right-of-way permits, and an erosion control plan; applicant is advised to respond in writing to obtain sign-off.

chapters.title: Closing Lakeview Farm Hearing
chapters.summary: Board closes the Lakeview Farm Inc. hearing after no further questions.

chapters.title: Spencer Pre-Application: Background
chapters.summary: Staff (Melinda) explains the history of a previously approved three-lot subdivision (Pumpkin Hill Road) where growth management allocation expired for Lot B, and outlines criteria for reinstating expired allocation.

chapters.title: Missing Documentation Recess
chapters.summary: Board realizes it lacks printed copies of key materials referenced by staff and takes a short recess to obtain them.

chapters.title: Re-review of Allocation Criteria
chapters.summary: Melinda repeats the criteria for reestablishing expired allocation (time limitation, substantial progress, conditions of approval, special findings) after the recess.

chapters.title: Conservation Commission's Open Space Concern
chapters.summary: Discussion reveals the conservation commission recommends protecting the southern half of Lot C (owned by a different, non-applicant party) as open space, raising a legal and procedural conundrum for the board.

chapters.title: Lot Ownership and Map Confusion
chapters.summary: Extensive back-and-forth clarifying which lot is which on the maps, boundary line adjustments, and confirming Lot B ownership by the Spencers versus Lot C ownership by another party.

chapters.title: Board Deliberates Path Forward
chapters.summary: Board debates whether to find substantial compliance and reestablish allocation, ignore or accommodate the conservation commission's recommendation on Lot C, seek a legal opinion, or continue the hearing to allow parties to work it out.

chapters.title: Growth Management Scoring Discussion
chapters.summary: Staff explains how growth management scoring and exemptions work, clarifying that losing this reinstatement path wouldn't necessarily preclude the applicant from getting allocation through competition.

chapters.title: Fire Department Comments and Closing
chapters.summary: Fire department driveway grade and fire pond recommendations are noted; board takes final questions and closes the Spencer hearing.

chapters.title: Mapletree Place Amendment Review
chapters.summary: Board reviews final plans for Mapletree Place amendment #2, covering pedestrian connections, crosswalks, bike racks, street trees, and landscaping within the Velco easement, before going into deliberation.

action_items.text: Add a written condition to the Lakeview Farm approval requiring the building envelope boundary shift that was previously discussed but omitted from the draft findings.
Provide a written response addressing Lisa Shelter's comments, including the erosion control plan, to obtain her sign-off on the final plans checklist.

Board to decide whether the Spencer/Pumpkin Hill Road subdivision is in substantial compliance with current development regulations, or seek a legal opinion, or continue the hearing a month to allow parties to resolve the Lot C open space issue.
Contact town staff in the morning to learn the board's decision on the pre-application.

bullets.text: Williston DRB met to review three items: a discretionary permit for Lakeview Farm Inc.'s two-lot split, a pre-application for reinstating expired growth management allocation for the Spencer property, and final plans review for Mapletree Place amendment #2.

Lakeview Farm Inc. two-lot subdivision met density and open space requirements (75% set-aside), with conservation commission recommending no required buffer on class 3 ponds and visual impact minimization for the new house.
Applicant's engineer confirmed the building envelope was moved 50 feet per prior board recommendation and additional plantings were added on Lot 1.
The Spencer pre-application involves reinstating one unit of expired growth management allocation for Lot B in a previously approved 3-lot, 90+ acre subdivision from 2008.
A major complication arose: the conservation commission recommends open space changes on Lot C, which is owned by a different party not present at the hearing and not part of this application.
Staff explained growth management scoring, noting the applicant might still qualify for allocation through competitive process or exemptions even without this reinstatement path.
Board closed the Lakeview Farm Inc. hearing (DP16-23) with a recommendation for approval largely intact, pending the added condition on building envelope.
Board closed the public hearing for the Spencer pre-application (DP17-30) to proceed to deliberation on the substantial compliance question.
Whether the board can or should enforce an open space change on Lot C, a lot not owned by the applicant and not part of the current application.

Whether the subdivision meets the 'substantial compliance with intent and purpose of current development regulations' criterion given changes in regulations (habitat assessment) since original approval.
Whether pausing to seek a legal opinion or continuing the hearing would affect the calendar-year deadline for the applicant to reapply.
Board to determine path forward on the Spencer application: find substantial compliance, seek legal opinion, or continue for a month to let parties work out the Lot C open space issue.
Board to continue deliberation on Mapletree Place amendment final plans, reviewing landscaping details near the Velco easement.
